text: Blessed is the one who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, who does not stand in the way of sinners, who does not sit in the seat of mockers,

versions.text: Blessed is the one who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, who does not stand in the way of sinners, who does not sit among the scoffers,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מוֹשַׁב (moshav) means "seat" or "session," indicating settled participation, not merely proximity ("among"). "Seat of mockers" preserves the escalating imagery (walk–stand–sit) and the definite-less Hebrew nouns, and it reads well aloud.

text: but whose delight is in the instruction of the LORD, and who murmurs over his instruction day and night.

versions.text: but whose delight is in the law of the LORD, and who meditates on his law day and night.
versions.explanation: תּוֹרָה is broader than "law" (teaching/instruction), and הָגָה denotes low recitation or murmuring, not silent reflection. If "law" is retained for familiarity, a footnote noting "instruction, teaching" and that meditating here involves speaking the words aloud would help readers.

text: He is like a tree transplanted beside channels of water, yielding its fruit in season, its leaf never withering; in all that he does, he thrives.

versions.text: He is like a tree planted by streams of water, that yields its fruit in season and whose leaves never wither. Whatever he does prospers.
versions.explanation: שָׁתוּל means deliberately transplanted (not merely growing wild), and פַּלְגֵי מָיִם suggests irrigation channels. The participial rhythm also flows better for oral reading than the relative clauses.

text: Not so the wicked. They are like chaff that the wind blows away.
Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.
For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.
